evidence_scope: uncommitted M2 working tree based on source_commit

toolchain.durability_interpretation: WAL and directory sync paths, restart recovery, index cache replacement, and suffix truncation were exercised; this is not physical power-loss evidence

commands.result: all M0 through M2 packages passed
all contract, M1 regression, segmented-storage, index-repair, and truncation tests passed
all M0 through M2 test packages passed under the race detector

acceptance.ST-06: small deterministic segments produce at least three WAL files; cross-boundary reads and restart return every record exactly once, and no frame crosses a segment
acceptance.ST-07: 80 deterministic random offset seeks across multi-record DATA and control-only segments match a reference log and report binary-search comparisons plus scanned WAL work
acceptance.ST-08: one missing and one corrupt index rebuild to the same reads while per-file SHA-256 digests prove WAL bytes are unchanged
acceptance.ST-09: an uncommitted suffix truncates with recomputed LEO/catalog/index and reuses provisional offsets; truncating at commit_index is rejected without changing WAL digests

seek_measurement.assertion: every individual seek scanned fewer than the 73432 bytes in the complete WAL

additional_results: An incomplete tail in a sealed segment fails closed; only the final active segment can be repaired.
A stable read-view lease excludes concurrent suffix truncation until the reader releases segment handles.
Injected sparse-index write failure does not roll back or fail a synced WAL append; restart rebuilds the stale cache.
Indexes are validated against anchors derived from WAL, so a CRC-valid but logically wrong cache is also replaced.
M1 SIGKILL, torn-active-tail, CRC, commit-floor, partial-write, sync-failure, hardstate, and data-dir identity tests remain green.
output_location: This scrubbed evidence manifest; deterministic seek metrics are emitted by TestM2ST07SparseSeekMatchesReferenceAndReportsWork under go test -v.
limitations: M2 stores per-frame position, term, kind, and DATA range metadata in memory, but record payloads are read from WAL through sparse anchors rather than loaded into a record map.
There is no retention, snapshot, compaction, or background index maintenance.
TruncateSuffix is a storage primitive only; no Raft implementation exists yet to authorize conflict truncation.
No network broker, Raft replication, ISR, public API, producer dedup, or group coordinator exists.
next_task: M3: implement per-partition full Raft with durable voting, elections, conflict reconciliation, current-term commit rules, NOOP ready barrier, ReadIndex, and RF1/RF3 process evidence.
